subject: science
skillName: Choosing the Best Material for a Job

items.prompt:
Some materials work better for a job because they have different
A) properties
B) names
C) owners
D) prices

steps: Different properties make materials suited for different jobs.

items.prompt:
The results of testing materials are called
A) data
B) colors
C) names
D) sounds

steps: Data are the results of a test.

items.prompt:
The best material for a raincoat
A) keeps water out
B) soaks up water
C) is the heaviest
D) is the reddest

steps: A raincoat must keep water out.

items.prompt:
For a chair leg that should not bend, the best material is one that is
A) soft
B) strong and stiff
C) soaks up water
D) bends easily

steps: A chair leg needs strength and should not bend.

items.prompt:
We look at data before choosing a material to
A) see which has the property the job needs
B) make it heavier
C) change its color
D) nothing
items.answer: A) see which has the property the job needs

steps: Data show which material suits the purpose.

items.prompt:
Which holds water best for a cup?
A) A paper towel
B) A plastic cup
C) A cloth
D) A net

steps: The plastic cup holds water without leaking.

items.prompt:
Two materials both keep water out for a raincoat, but one is stiff and one bends. The better one is
A) the stiff one
B) the bendable one, because a raincoat must move with the person
C) neither
D) the heavier one
items.answer: B) the bendable one, because a raincoat must move with the person

steps: A raincoat needs to keep water out and also bend.

items.prompt:
The BEST way to pick a material for a strong bridge model is to
A) guess
B) add weight to each and see which holds the most without breaking
C) pick the prettiest
D) pick the cheapest
items.answer: B) add weight to each and see which holds the most without breaking

steps: Testing with weight is the data that shows the strongest.
